name: Chemoinformatics
tagline: AI-driven prediction, QSAR/QSPR modeling, and molecular data intelligence.
seo_title: Chemoinformatics — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Chemoinformatics on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in molecular representations, QSAR/QSPR, chemical databases and virtual screening.

definition.lead: Chemoinformatics applies information science to chemistry: representing molecules as data, storing and searching them, and predicting their properties.
definition.body: It powers chemical databases, similarity searches, QSAR and QSPR models and virtual screening. Every time a model predicts solubility or toxicity from a structure, chemoinformatics is at work.

timeline.title: QSAR
timeline.text: Corwin Hansch and Toshio Fujita relate biological activity to physical properties of substituents.

timeline.title: The Morgan algorithm
timeline.text: Harry Morgan publishes a method to give molecules a unique description.
timeline.why: Still behind the popular Morgan fingerprints.

timeline.title: SMILES
timeline.text: David Weininger publishes a line notation for molecules.
timeline.why: A compact way to write molecules that computers can read.

timeline.title: PubChem
timeline.text: The US National Institutes of Health launch PubChem.
timeline.why: A free database of chemical structures and bioassays.

timeline.title: InChI
timeline.why: A standard, non-proprietary identifier for chemical substances.

timeline.title: ChEMBL
timeline.text: ChEMBL is launched as an open database of bioactive molecules.
timeline.why: Millions of activity measurements for modelling.

timeline.title: Extended-connectivity fingerprints
timeline.text: David Rogers and Mathew Hahn publish the ECFP method.
timeline.why: One of the most widely used molecular fingerprints.

timeline.title: MoleculeNet
timeline.text: A benchmark suite for molecular machine learning is published.
timeline.why: Common datasets to compare models fairly.
